metaDescription: North Hobbs sits over some of Lea County's most active Delaware Basin acreage. Get a real valuation on your mineral or royalty interest.
heroLead: Hobbs itself is Lea County's largest city, and North Hobbs, the unincorporated stretch just outside the city limits, sits over acreage that's been in nearly continuous development for the past decade.
intro: I've bought interests all over Lea County, and North Hobbs tends to surprise owners the most, because it's close enough to town that people assume it's built out and drilled dry. It isn't. Horizontal Wolfcamp and Bone Spring units keep going in around the northern edge of Hobbs, and a lot of small legacy interests out there have quietly become more valuable than the owner realizes.

sections.heading: Urban edge, oilfield core
paragraphs: North Hobbs sits at the boundary between residential and commercial growth spilling out of Hobbs proper and the ranch and oilfield acreage that surrounds it. That mix means some tracts here have surface development on them — storage yards, service company lots, the occasional subdivision — while the minerals underneath are still leased and produced through the same horizontal units common across Lea County.

sections.heading: Why proximity to Hobbs matters for your interest
paragraphs: Because Hobbs is a hub for oilfield services, operators working this part of Lea County have easy access to workforce, equipment, and infrastructure, which tends to support continued development rather than a boom that fades once the initial rush passes. That's a reasonable factor in favor of near-term activity if your minerals sit in this corridor.

sections.heading: Getting a real number, not a guess
paragraphs: I pull current permits and completions near your specific tract before I ever talk numbers, because 'North Hobbs' covers enough ground that two nearby interests can have very different outlooks depending on which unit they're pooled into. Send whatever paperwork you have and I'll tell you honestly where you stand.

faqs.question: Is North Hobbs still an active drilling area, or has it slowed down since it's so close to town?
faqs.answer: It remains active. Proximity to Hobbs actually supports continued development, since operators have easy access to workforce and infrastructure there. We check current permits on your specific tract to confirm.

faqs.question: There's a business or storage lot on the surface above my minerals. Does that change anything?
faqs.answer: Not for your mineral ownership. Surface use and mineral rights are separate, and production can continue underneath developed surface acreage through standard horizontal drilling.

faqs.question: How quickly can you make an offer on a North Hobbs interest?
faqs.answer: Usually within a few days of receiving your documentation, after we've checked title basics and current activity near your tract.
